revisionNote: The capture baselines for frame, top background, category icon row and item label row were re-measured after the firmware particle simulation landed (src/particles.cpp pool port): the dust now renders where the reference frame has its own particles at a different phase, so those four layers moved by <0.011 SSIM and <0.1 dB. The stored-pair baselines above remain the historical numbers.

baselinePair.note: Stored 1920x1080 native capture of the settled Game root menu, scored against the stored RPCS3 frame. This pair is the historical baseline: whole frame 18.20 dB / 0.8388 SSIM. Offline scoring of this pair is deterministic, so its gate catches tooling (decoder/metric/crop) regressions.

tolerance.rationale: Two canonical capture runs are pixel-identical (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000), so run-to-run jitter contributes nothing. The budget therefore only absorbs GPU/driver shader noise and small environment drift. 0.5 dB PSNR is a 12% MSE increase, while a visible layer regression (a moved icon, a dropped label row, a shifted gradient) moves a layer score by more than 1 dB; 0.004 SSIM is likewise far above observed noise and far below a visible regression.

capture.note: Canonical capture recipe. All animation clocks are pinned, so two runs are pixel-identical. XMB_STEAM_ROOT points at an empty directory: the stored RPCS3 reference frame's Game column predates this PC's Steam library and shows the dev_flash XMBML entries only. backgroundClock 10:00 is the traced daytime mapping used by the stored baseline; uiClock matches the reference frame's 25/10 12:32.

stateSelfBaseline.rationale: Named states have no RPCS3 frame: their reference is the deterministic native render itself, so a fresh capture must reproduce that frame (self-baseline regression gate, not firmware fidelity). Two runs of every state are byte-identical on this machine (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000). 55 dB still catches any deterministic drawing change (one changed 255-level pixel already costs ~68 dB on a 1080p frame) while leaving room for GPU/driver shader noise; 0.9995 SSIM is the same margin. Refresh a reference deliberately after an intended rendering change with --states --save-reference.
